articles.title: Protect Skin and Comfort During Care at Home
articles.description: Practical prompts for discussing pressure relief, skin checks and an individual wound-care plan with the patient's healthcare team.
articles.body:
## Start with an individual plan
Agree an individual repositioning and pressure-relief plan with the patient's healthcare team. The appropriate plan depends on the person's condition and needs.

## Check skin and comfort
Check skin, moisture and comfort. Report persistent redness or broken skin to the healthcare team rather than treating this short guide as an individual wound-care prescription.

## Follow the agreed care plan
Use the support surface and wound-care plan advised for the patient. Ask the treating team if the plan is unclear or the skin changes.

## Important note
This patient-education draft supports discussion with a clinician and does not replace individual assessment.

articles.title: Supporting Stroke Recovery and Safer Swallowing
articles.description: Follow the person's swallowing assessment, use the prescribed food textures and recognise when feeding must stop and help is needed.
articles.body:
## Follow the swallowing assessment
Follow the swallowing assessment and the food textures prescribed for the individual. Do not independently change a person's prescribed food or fluid texture.

## Support a safe position
Support an upright, comfortable position for meals, in line with the person's care plan.

## Stop and seek help when warning signs occur
Stop feeding and seek help for choking, new breathlessness or reduced alertness. Do not force food or fluid when swallowing may be unsafe.

## Important note
This draft is based on the existing patient-facing guidance and must be reviewed before being used as a standalone clinical education article.

articles.title: Living With Kidney Disease: Follow an Individual Care Plan
articles.description: Keep dialysis, medicine and blood-test appointments, and ask the kidney team for personal fluid, salt and potassium guidance.
articles.body:
## Keep planned follow-up
Keep dialysis, medicine and blood-test appointments, and discuss missed appointments with the treating team.

## Ask for individual dietary guidance
Ask the healthcare team for the fluid, salt and potassium plan that applies to the individual. Requirements vary with kidney function, test results and dialysis treatment; a general article cannot set a personal limit.

## Do not change dialysis independently
Changes to dialysis frequency belong with the nephrology team. Contact the treating service when advice is unclear or the person's condition changes.

## Important note
This draft is educational and does not replace an individual kidney-care plan.

articles.title: Making the Home Safer for Older Adults
articles.description: Simple home-safety prompts covering clear walkways, comfortable lighting, footwear, mobility aids and reporting falls or new confusion.
articles.body:
## Reduce everyday hazards
Keep walkways clear and lighting comfortable at night. Review footwear, mobility aids and bathroom supports with the person and their care team.

## Report changes
Report a fall or new confusion. These changes can have different causes and need appropriate assessment; do not assume they are an inevitable part of ageing.

## Individualise the plan
Choose home-safety changes around the person's mobility, environment and assessed needs. Ask the healthcare team if additional support is needed.

## Important note
This draft is adapted from the existing patient-facing section and requires standalone clinical review before publication.
